source_text: Ἐξανατείλας οὖν ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἔτι πᾶν ξύλον, ὡραῖον εἰς ὅρασιν καὶ καλὸν εἰς βρῶσιν. Ἐν γὰρ πρώτοις μόνα ᾖν τὰ ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ γεγενημένα, φυτὰ καὶ σπέρματα καὶ χλόαι· τὰ δὲ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ ἐγενήθη διαφόρῳ καλλονῇ καὶ ὡραιότητι, ὅκου γε καὶ φυτεία ὠνόμασται ὑπὸ θεοῦ πεφυτευμένη. Καὶ τὰ μὲν λοιπὰ φυτὰ ὅμοια καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἔσχηκεν· τὰ δὲ δύο ξύλα, τὸ τῆς ζωῆς καὶ τὸ τῆς γνώσεως, οὐκ ἔσχηκεν ἑτέρα γῆ ἀλλ᾿ ἢ ἐν μόνῳ τῷ παραδείσῳ.Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ὁ παράδεισος γῆ ἐστιν καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς πεφύτευται, ἡ γραφὴ λέγει· Καὶ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ θεὸς παράδεισον ἐν Ἐδὲμ κατὰ ἀντολάς, καὶ ἔθετο ἐκεῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον· καὶ ἐξανέτειλεν ὁ θεὸς ἔτι ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς πᾶν ξύλον, ὡραῖον εἰς ὅρασιν καὶ καλὸν εἰς βρῶσιν. Τὸ οὖν ἔτι ἐκ τῆς γῆς καὶ κατὰ ἀνατολὰς σαφῶς διδάσκει ἡμᾶς ἡ θεία γραφὴ τὸν παράδεισον ὑπὸ τοῦτον τὸν οὐρανόν, ὑφ᾿ ὃν καὶ ἀνατολαὶ καὶ· γῆ εἰσιν. Ἐδὲμ δὲ ἑβραϊστὶ τὸ εἰρημένον ἑρμηνεύεται τρυφή. Ποταμὸν δὲ σεσήμακεν ἐκπορεύεσθαι ἐξ Ἐδὲμ ποτίζειν τὸν παράδεισον, κἀκεῖθεν διαχωρίζεσθαι εἰς τέσσαρας ἀρχάς· ὧν δύο, οἱ καλούμενοι Φεισὼν καὶ Γεών, ποτίζουσιν τὰ ἀνατολικὰ μέρη, μάλιστα ὁ Γεών, ὁ κυκλῶν πᾶσαν γῆν Αἰθιοπίας, ὅν φασιν ἐν τῇ Αἰγύπτῳ ἀναφαίνεσθαι τὸν καλούμενον Νεῖλον. Οἱ δὲ ἄλλοι δύο ποταμοὶ φανερῶς γινώσκονται παρ᾿ ἡμῖν, οἱ καλούμενοι Τίγρις καὶ Εὐφράτης· οὗτοι γὰρ γειτνιῶσιν ἕως τῶν ἡμετέρων κλιμάτων.Θεὶς δὲ ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καθὼς προειρήκαμεν, ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ εἰς τὸ ἐργάζεσθαι καὶ φυλάσσειν αὐτόν, ἐνετείλατο αὐτῷ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν καρπῶν ἐσθίειν, δηλονότι καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ τῆς ζωῆς, μόνου δὲ ἐκ τοῦ ξύλου τοῦ τῆς γνώσεως ἐνετείλατο αὐτῷ μὴ γεύσασθαι. Μετέθηκεν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῆς γῆς, ἐξ ἧς ἐγεγόνει, εἰς τὸν παράδεισον, διδοὺς αὐτῷ ἀφορμὴν προκοπῆς, ὅπως αὐξάνων καὶ τέλειος γενόμενος, ἔτι δὲ καὶ θεὸς ἀναδειχθείς, οὕτως καὶ εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀναβῇ (μέσος γὰρ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐγεγόνει, οὔτε θνητὸς ὁλοσχερῶς οὔτε ἀθάνατος τὸ καθόλου, δεκτικὸς δὲ ἑκατέρων· οὕτως καὶ τὸ χωρίον ὁ παράδεισος, ὡς πρὸς καλλονήν, μέσος τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γεγένηται), ἔχων ἀϊδιότητα. Τὸ δὲ εἰπεῖν ἐργάζεσθαι οὐκ ἄλλην τινὰ ἐργασίαν δηλοῖ ἀλλ᾿ ἢ τὸ φυλάσσειν τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅκως μὴ παρακούσας ἀπολέσῃ ἑαυτόν, καθὼς καὶ ἀπώλεσεν διὰ ἁμαρτίας.
pass_a_gloss: So God brought forth from the earth every tree that is pleasing to the sight and good for food. For at first, only the things that were made on the third day existed, namely plants and seeds and grasses. But the things in Paradise were made with a different beauty and loveliness, so that even the planting was named by God as planted by Him. The rest of the plants are similar and the world has them, but the two trees, the tree of life and the tree of knowledge, no other earth has except only in Paradise alone. The scripture says that Paradise is a earth and is planted on the earth, for it says: And God planted a Paradise in Eden towards the east, and He put the man there, and God brought forth from the earth every tree that is pleasing to the sight and good for food. The fact that it is from the earth and towards the east clearly teaches us, according to the divine scripture, that Paradise is under this heaven, under which there are also easts and earth. Eden, which is said in Hebrew, is interpreted as luxury. And a river was made to flow out from Eden to water Paradise, and from there it is divided into four heads, of which two, called Phison and Geon, water the eastern parts, especially Geon, which circles all the earth of Ethiopia, which they say appears in Egypt as the Nile. The other two rivers are clearly known to us, called Tigris and Euphrates, for they border up to our climates. And God, having put the man in Paradise, as we previously said, to work and to guard it, commanded him to eat from all the fruits, clearly also from the tree of life, but only from the tree of knowledge He commanded him not to taste. And God transferred him from the earth from which he was made into Paradise, giving him an opportunity for progress, so that growing and becoming perfect, and also becoming a god, he might ascend into heaven, for the man was made middle, neither entirely mortal nor immortal, but capable of both, and so also the place Paradise was made middle, as to beauty, of the world and heaven, having eternity. To say 'to work' does not indicate any other work except to guard the commandment of God, so that not disobeying he might not destroy himself, as he also destroyed himself through sin.

bible_refs.note: And God planted a Paradise in Eden towards the east, and He put the man there, and God brought forth from the earth every tree that is pleasing to the sight and good for food.

pass_b_english: God caused every tree that is pleasing to the sight and good for food to spring from the earth. At the beginning only the vegetation created on the third day existed—plants, seeds, and grasses—yet the growth in Paradise was fashioned with a distinct beauty and loveliness, so that the very planting was called by God a planting of His own. The rest of the plants are like those the world possesses, but the two trees, the tree of life and the tree of knowledge, are found nowhere else but in Paradise alone. Scripture teaches that Paradise is a land planted on the earth, for it says that God planted a paradise in Eden toward the east, set the man there, and made every tree pleasing to the sight and good for food rise from the earth (Genesis 2:8-10). The phrase “from the earth” and “toward the east” shows that Paradise lies beneath this heaven, under which both east and earth exist. Eden, in Hebrew, means luxury. A river flows out of Eden to water Paradise and then splits into four branches; two of them, Phison and Geon, irrigate the eastern regions, especially Geon, which encircles all the land of Ethiopia and is identified with the Nile in Egypt. The other two rivers, the Tigris and the Euphrates, are well known to us because they reach our own lands. God placed the man in Paradise, as previously noted, to cultivate and guard it, commanding him to eat from every fruit—including the tree of life—but forbidding him to taste of the tree of knowledge. God transferred the man from the earth from which he was formed into Paradise, granting him a chance for advancement so that, as he grew and became perfect and even divine, he might ascend to heaven; for man was created as a middle being, neither wholly mortal nor wholly immortal, but capable of both, and Paradise itself, in its beauty, stands midway between the world and heaven, possessing eternity. The command “to work” signifies no labor other than keeping God’s commandment, so that by not disobeying he would not destroy himself, as he ultimately did through sin.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that preserves all nuances, including the theological distinction of man as a 'middle' being (μέσος) and the purpose of the transfer to Paradise. Scripture citations (Genesis 2:8-10) are correctly applied to the quoted content.

Pass A: 'And God brought forth from the earth every tree that is pleasing to the sight and good for food.' Pass B: 'God caused every tree that is pleasing to the sight and good for food to spring from the earth.'
